..
Issued at 356 AM EDT Fri Sep 11 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Rather quick flow across the northern tier of the country 
attm...with 100-120kt upper jet axes from WA to Manitoba ahead of a 
positively tilted trough axis over western Canada...and from the 
Lower Great Lakes northeastward into ME ahead of another elongated 
positively tilted trough axis stretching from the Central Plains to 
the OH Valley. Deepest absolute moisture (pwats greater than 1.5-
2in) ahead of the latter feature across the SE US and Gulf Coast, 
and its attendant surface front draped from TX to OH up toward Boston
     though some Pacific moisture (pwats 1-1.5in) is located along and 
ahead of the former, from the Northern Plains to Manitoba/Ontario, 
and down into the Upper Midwest. Mid-level warming and upper-level 
cooling resulting in steepening lapse rates across the northern 
Plains, with cooling aloft steepening lapse rates beneath the trough 
axis itself over western Canada. Cold baroclinic zone/surface 
boundary stretches from central Canada to the PacNW (where a nice 
baroclinic leaf is evident on satellite imagery over WA, attendant 
to a PV max digging in from the Pacific), and warm baroclinic zone, 
from Manitoba down into the Upper Midwest/Central Plains...with 
850mb temps in the teens and 20s across the Plains. Return flow 
developing across the Plains/southern Canada around surface ridge in 
the Upper Great Lakes...resulting in a maximum of warm advection 
across Ontario/Manitoba, shunting the pool of 0C 850mb air eastward 
across James Bay. In the meantime, beneath said surface ridge and 
abundant subsidence...we are calm, dry, and cool...with temperatures 
dropping back into the upper 40s and lower 50s as of 3z under clear 
skies. 

Upper ridge axis builds overhead today, with generally quiet 
conditions expected, though return flow will be strengthening ahead 
of upstream perturbations. This should also lead to some warm 
advection cloud cover drifting through today. The upstream trough 
axis will approach late tonight into Saturday, dragging a SW-NE 
oriented surface trough eastward across the Upper Midwest, resulting 
in even stronger return flow on Saturday, and think some convective 
activity will be around the Midwest into Ontario during this 
timeframe, most likely impacting our area later Saturday into 
Saturday night as the trough axis sweeps by to our north, while OH 
Valley activity likely remains to our south. Hot on its heels, 
however, is another perturbation over the Canadian Prairies, which 
currently looks to dig a little deeper into the Great Lakes than the 
first system, keeping things active early Sunday...and bringing some 
cooler air into play. We could see a brief break in the action 
Monday, unless warm advection convection rears its head...and warm 
advection will certainly be a concern ahead of a sharper PV maxima 
digging across the US/Canadian border upstream Monday. This 
currently looks to pass by the area Monday night into Tuesday, and a 
notable concern with this is that signals currently point toward a 
wide-open Gulf and subsequently, potential for deep moisture and 
heavy rainfall in the Upper Midwest. Southwesterly flow aloft 
generally looks to persist across the eastern US/Great Lakes into 
the latter half of the week, with additional perturbations in the 
northern stream trying to affect us toward Wednesday/Thursday, 
though quite a bit of uncertainty attm in the details/timing of 
these. Overall, expect active weather off and on through the course 
of the next week.  

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/storm chances tonight into Saturday... Non zero chance some 
activity could sneak in toward Saginaw Bay Saturday morning on the 
very northern edge of the OH Valley system's influence, noting 
signals for an increase in low-level moisture...and there are some 
signals for a subtle positively tilted PV maxima to slip through 
around 12-15z...though not sure if this will be enough to generate 
precip or not. Primary concern tonight/Saturday morning will be how 
quickly the upstream warm advection precip moves in from the 
W/NW...and given that we are likely to stay quite dry in the low-
levels today, think onset of rain will be a tad slower. Most likely 
chance of anything getting in during the early morning would be for 
the EUP and perhaps Straits. Better chance for rain/storms would be 
in the afternoon and evening from west to east along/ahead of the 
front, particularly toward the EUP and NE Lower where there is 
potential for somewhat deeper moisture and better influence of 
synoptic forcing from the PV max...and where there are signals for 
an increase in low-level fgen toward 18-0z. 

Rain/storm chances Saturday night into Sunday... Current expectation 
is for temps to fall rather dramatically behind the front Saturday 
night, with 850mb temps approaching 4-5C or colder by 12z Sunday. 
This should result in at least some daytime instability, if not 
overlake instability..
